text.text: Outbound: how does an approved email draft get sent through Gmail?
New engineers · Email branch of sendMessage: owner clicks Send, row is claimed, guards run, Gmail sends, status is written.

Key: frames = trust/deployment zones; box = runtime actor/process; cylinder = stored state; double border = external service.
Arrows: caller → recipient, response included; solid = sync. Flow type is also written on each arrow.

Only draft/failed outbound rows are
claimed as 'sending' (edits saved);
others return skipped, so a double click
sends once. A crash mid-send can leave
a row stuck in 'sending'.

Daily limit fails the row. The prior-reply
check is fail-open (errors count as 0).
The Gmail in-touch check fails closed,
skipped for replies or owner override;
hits are saved.

No usable/bounced email, no Gmail
connection, or a send error marks the
row failed (send errors also recorded as
a Gmail connection error). Failed rows
can be claimed again.
Outside this view: LinkedIn sends via the browser worker; X DMs marked sent by hand; Finding, research, enrollment and the reply-check cron.
